subject_entity.notes: Samaritan sorcerer mentioned in Acts 8:9–24; regarded by Irenaeus and Justin as the father of all heresies and root of Gnosticism. He claimed to be the supreme divine Power. His companion Helena he called the first divine Thought (Ennoia). Opposed by Peter at Samaria.

object_entity.description: The Church accepts the Old Testament as authoritative Christian scripture; the God of creation and Israel is the same God as the Father of Jesus Christ. Denied by Marcion, Valentinus, Basilides, and most Gnostic schools.

evidence.notes: Simon's system posits a supreme Power distinct from the creator, implicitly opposing OT God.

passage.excerpt: Simon the Samaritan was that magician of whom Luke, the disciple and follower of the apostles, writes in Acts. He claimed to be the supreme divine Power, the father of all heresy. Having purchased a certain woman named Helena, he declared her to be the first Conception of his mind, the mother of all, through whom he had originally conceived the creation of angels and archangels.
